newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican daily port, shipping update for Dec. 19.
newsitem.headline: Mexican daily port, shipping update for Dec. 19.

text.p: Ten Gulf of Mexico ports, including Mexico's three main crude ports, were shut Thursday as of 1000 local/1600 GMT, the Communications and Transport Ministry said in a daily update.
Pajaritos, Dos Bocas and Cayo Arcas were shut for the second day, preventing any crude exporting ships from sailing.

At Pajaritos, winds were reported at between 60 and 70 km per hour on Thursday, and at Dos Bocas officials said wind speeds were dying down to 50 and 60 km per hour. Winds at Cayo Arcas were clocked between 85 and 95 km per hour, port officials said.
Other ports reported closed in the bulletin included:

Altamira, Tampico and Tuxpan in Tamaulipas state, Veracruz and Coatzacoalcos in Veracruz state, Frontera in Tabasco state, Ciudad del Carmen and Campeche in Campeche state and Progreso in Yucatan state.
La Paz, Ensenada and Rosarito on the Pacific coast and Puerto Juarez and Cozumel on the Yucatan peninsula prohibited smaller ships from sailing, the report said.
The ministry updated port conditions and shipping warnings for the Gulf of Mexico, Caribbean and Pacific Coast.

Cloudy with moderate rains along the coast of the states of Jalisco, Colima, Michoacan, Guerrero and Oaxaca. Winds below 10 knots (19 km/11 miles per hour) with waves reaching three to five feet high.
In the Gulf of Tehuantepec north and northeast winds were clocked at 40 to 50 knots (76 to 95 km/44 to 55 miles per hour) with wave heights at nine to 12 feet.

Cold front heading toward Yucatan peninsula to the state of Chiapas, bringing lower temperatures, clouds and moderate to strong rains along the Gulf of Mexico. Winds from the north at 35 to 45 knots (67 to 86 km/38 to 49 miles per hour) with wind gusts up to 104 km/61 miles per hour and waves of 12 to 16 feet high. Storm conditions expected to ease later in the day in the northern gulf region.

High winds along central Caribbean. Winds and rains along coasts of Panama, Costa Rica and Nicaragua of 10 to 15 knots (19 to 28 km/11 to 17 miles per hour) and waves of between three and five feet high.
